Stewart Jr.''' (born July 28, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Saski Baskonia]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State Bulldogs]]. ==High school career== Stewart attended [[Riverside High School (Mississippi)|Riverside High School]] in [[Avon, Mississippi]]. As a freshman, Stewart averaged 15.2 points, 6.4 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game. In his sophomore season, he averaged 17.4 points, 6.2 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game.{{Cite web |title=D.J. Stewart Jr.: 2021 Draft Prospect |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/dj-stewart-jr-2021-draft-prospect |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |accessdate=July 30, 2021}} Entering his junior season, he did not receive any [[NCAA Division I]] offers.{{Cite web |last=Lowery |first=Logan |date=January 21, 2020 |title=Stewart attains goal through hard work |url=https://www.djournal.com/sports/stewart-attains-goal-through-hard-work/article_b3022d8e-a7d6-5f1e-98a6-90577699c9d5.html |access-date=July 30, 2021 |website=[[Northeast Mississippi Daily Journal]]}} As a junior, Stewart averaged 18.9 points, 9.7 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game. He averaged 25.3 points, 10.7 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game and was named All-State by ''[[The Clarion-Ledger]]'' in his senior season.{{Cite web |title=D.J. Stewart Jr. - Men's Basketball |url=https://hailstate.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/d-j--stewart-jr-/6188 |access-date=July 30, 2021 |website=Mississippi State University Athletics}}{{Cite web |last=Capers |first=Joshua |date=April 1, 2021 |title=Mississippi State basketball second-leading scorer DJ Stewart Jr to enter name in NBA Draft |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/2021/04/01/mississippi-state-basketball-dj-stewart-jr-nba-draft-msu-bulldogs/4838516001/ |access-date=July 30, 2021 |website=[[The Clarion-Ledger]]}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]] over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] and [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]].{{Cite web |last=Sammon |first=Will |date=July 25, 2017 |title=Mississippi State hoops adds another in four-star SF D.J. Stewart |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/mississippi-state-hoops-adds-another-in-four-star-sf-d-j-stewart |access-date=July 30, 2021 |website=USA Today High School Sports}} He was rated a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]].{{Cite web |last=Bossi |first=Eric |date=July 24, 2017 |title=Mississippi State scores again, 4-star D.J. Stewart makes call |url=https://n.rivals.com/news/mississippi-state-scores-again-4-star-d-j-stewart-makes-call |access-date=July 30, 2021 |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]]}} ==College career== Stewart [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his first season at Mississippi State because head coach [[Ben Howland]] did not expect him to receive significant playing time. As a freshman, he averaged 8.5 points and 2.5 rebounds per game.{{Cite web |last=Faulk |first=Robbie |date=January 5, 2021 |title=DJ Stewart emerging as offensive force after Mizzou performance |url=https://247sports.com/college/mississippi-state/Article/DJ-Stewart-Mississippi-State-mens-basketball--158643249/ |access-date=July 30, 2021 |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]]}} On December 12, 2020, Stewart scored a career-high 32 points in an 85–82 double overtime loss to [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]].{{Cite magazine |last=Coleman |first=Joel |date=December 12, 2020 |title=Missed free throws haunt Mississippi State in loss to Dayton |url=https://www.si.com/college/mississippistate/basketball/dayton-postgame-recap-121220 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 30, 2021}} As a sophomore, he averaged 16 points, 3.4 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game.{{Cite web |last=Middleton |first=Dalton |date=April 1, 2021 |title=Mississippi State's D.J. Stewart to test NBA Draft process |url=https://www.djournal.com/sports/college/mississippi-state/mississippi-states-d-j-stewart-to-test-nba-draft-process/article_2763e8ef-e78b-5087-a90c-f80fc5c1a114.html |access-date=July 30, 2021 |website=[[Northeast Mississippi Daily Journal]]}} He earned Second Team All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) honors from the league's coaches.{{Cite web |last=Coleman |first=Joel |date=March 9, 2021 |title=Stewart and Ado pick up SEC yearly honors |url=https://www.si.com/college/mississippistate/basketball/stewart-ado-sec-yearly-mbb-honors-3921 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} Stewart was one of three finalists for the [[Howell Trophy]].{{Cite web |last=Dunaway |first=Matt |date=May 10, 2021 |title=Stewart Jr. Named Bailey Howell Trophy Finalist |url=https://hailstate.com/news/2021/5/10/mens-basketball-stewart-jr-named-bailey-howell-trophy-finalist.aspx |access-date=July 30, 2021 |website=Mississippi State University Athletics}} On April 1, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility. He later signed with an [[sports agent|agent]], forgoing his remaining eligibility.{{Cite web |last=Hodge |first=Garrick |date=May 13, 2021 |title=Report: D.J. Stewart to stay in NBA draft, will not return to Mississippi State |url=https://cdispatch.com/sports/2021-05-13/report-d-j-stewart-to-stay-in-nba-draft-will-not-return-to-mississippi-state/ |access-date=July 30, 2021 |website=[[The Commercial Dispatch]]}} ==Professional career== ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2021–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Stewart joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite news |last=Suss |first=Nick |date=July 30, 2021 |title=Mississippi State guard D.J. Stewart Jr. gets free agent deal with Miami Heat |work=[[Clarion Ledger]] |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/mississippi-state/2021/07/30/dj-stewart-miami-heat-nba-draft-2021-mississippi-state-guard-prospect/8070027002/ |access-date=August 3, 2021}} On August 17, 2021, he signed with the Heat.{{Cite web |date=August 17, 2021 |title=HEAT Signs D.J. Stewart |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-dj-stewart |access-date=August 18, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} Stewart was waived before the start of the season and joined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web |title=Skyforce Announces 2021-22 Training Camp Roster |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/skyforce-announces-2021-22-training-camp-roster/n-5758534 |website=Our Sports Central |access-date=October 27, 2021 |date=October 26, 2021}} === Austin Spurs (2022) === On March 4, 2022, Stewart signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.poundingtherock.com/2022/3/4/22962268/the-spurs-have-signed-robert-woodard-ii-and-d-j-stewart-jr-to-two-way-contracts|website=poundingtherock.com|title=The Spurs have signed Robert Woodard II and D.J. Stewart Jr. to two-way contracts|date=March 4, 2022|access-date=March 4, 2022}} However, Stewart did not appear in any one of the games for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] but only played for there affiliated team [[Austin Spurs]]. === Sioux Falls Skyforce (2022–2023) === On September 21, 2022, the [[Dallas Mavericks]] announced that they had signed Stewart.{{cite web |last1=Sefko |first1=Eddie |date=September 21, 2022 |title=Mavericks fill out training camp roster with five signees |url=https://www.mavs.com/camp-signees-2/ |access-date=September 21, 2022 |website=mavs.com}} He was waived before the start of the season on October 13, 2022.{{cite web | last=Amico | first=Sam | title=Mavs Waive Tyler Hall, DJ Stewart, Marcus Bingham, Mouhamadou Gueye | website=Hoops Wire | date=2022-10-13 | url=https://hoopswire.com/mavs-waive-tyler-hall-dj-stewart-marcus-bingham-mouhamadou-gueye/ | access-date=2025-11-22}} and on October 24, 2022, rejoined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] roster.{{cite web|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-training-camp-roster-ahead-of-2022-23-season/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=SKYFORCE ANNOUNCES TRAINING CAMP ROSTER AHEAD OF 2022-23 SEASON|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022}} ===Marineros de Puerto Plata (2023)=== On May 1, 2023, Stewart signed with the [[Marineros de Puerto Plata]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto]] until the end of the season.{{cite web|first=Hector|last=Garcia Sr.|title=Marineros de Puerto Plata anuncian tres refuerzos LNB 2023|url=https://momentodeportivord.com/marineros-de-puerto-plata-anuncian-tres-refuerzos-lnb-2023/|website=MomentoDeportivoRD.com|date=May 1, 2023|access-date=June 8, 2023|language=Spanish}} ===Cedevita Olimpija (2023–2026)=== On September 22, 2023, Stewart signed a one-year deal with [[KK Cedevita Olimpija|Cedevita Olimpija]].{{cite web|title=D. J. Stewart Jr. joins Cedevita Olimpija before the start of the regular season|url=https://cedevita.olimpija.com/en/d-j-stewart-jr-joins-cedevita-olimpija-before-the-start-of-the-regular-season/|website=Cedevita.Olimpija.com|date=September 22, 2023|access-date=September 22, 2023|language=en-GB}} On June 15, 2024, he signed a new contract for two more years.{{Cite web |date=2024-06-15 |title=DJ Stewart ostaja v Ljubljani! |url=https://cedevita.olimpija.com/dj-stewart-ostaja-v-ljubljani/ |access-date=2024-06-18 |website=KK Cedevita Olimpija, Ljubljana |language=sl-SI}} ===Baskonia (2026–present)=== On June 28, 2026, Stewart signed a two-season deal with [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |date=2026-06-28 |title=Dewayne Stewart Jr, primera pieza del nuevo Kosner Baskonia |url=https://www.baskonia.com/es/noticias/dewayne-stewart-jr-primera-pieza-del-nuevo-kosner-baskonia |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=baskonia.com |language=es}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} {| class=wikitable |- |style="background:#cfecec;
